use_case: The agent has to commit and push a parser fix and open a PR. It must follow the AGENTS.md conventions and leave out files that were already dirty before the session started.
situation: In an agricultural telemetry pipeline, the agent fixed the timezone handling in the soil-moisture parser for ticket AGRO-412. The early git status showed two files that were already dirty and are unrelated to the task. AGENTS.md sets the commit format, requires sign-off, and says PRs target develop.
must_keep: The AGENTS.md excerpt with the commit format (pt-BR, Refs footer, -s sign-off, PR to develop). Also the initial git status, which shows config/sensores.local.yaml and scripts/dump_tmp.py were dirty before any edits.
may_drop: The legacy CONTRIBUTING doc, the git log with mixed commit styles, the grep and test outputs, the edit diffs, the final git status and the timezone chatter.
why_judges_fail: The final git status and the recent git log look more relevant to committing. But the final status mixes session files with pre-existing ones, and the log and legacy doc show conventions that are wrong. Only the early blocks make it possible to stage the right files and format the commit and PR correctly.
